A: Did you make a (　) at the restaurant?

A: Could you tell me (　) to use this machine?

items.q:
A: Excuse me. I bought this shirt yesterday, but it's too small.
B: (　)
A: Yes, here it is.

items.ex: A が「はい、これです」と何かを渡しているので、レシートを持っているかたずねています。

items.q:
A: Are you going to the party on Saturday, Jim?
B: I'd like to, but (　)

items.q:
A: Mom, I'm going to ride my bike to the lake.
B: OK, but (　)
A: Don't worry. I always do.
items.ex: 「心配しないで。いつもそうしてるよ」と答えているので、ヘルメットをかぶるよう注意しています。

items.q:
A: How did you like the new Thai restaurant?
B: The food was great, (　)
A: Really? I'll call before I go.
items.ex: 「行く前に電話する(予約する)」と答えているので、混んでいたことがわかります。

items.q:
A: I'm thinking of buying a new smartphone.
B: (　)
A: Mine is five years old, and the battery dies quickly.
o: Why do you need a new one?
items.ex: A が古くて電池がすぐ切れると理由を答えているので、Why(なぜ)の質問です。

blocks.title: A Library for Tools
blocks.body:
In some towns in the United States and Canada, people can borrow tools such as drills, ladders, and garden tools from a "tool library." These libraries work like normal libraries. Members can take a tool home for a week and then return it.
Many people need a drill only once or twice a year, so buying one can be a waste of money. Tool libraries ( 21 ). Members can use many kinds of tools without spending much money, and they do not need space at home to keep them.
Tool libraries also bring people together. Volunteers often teach classes on how to fix chairs or build shelves. Some members say that they have made new friends there. ( 22 ), tool libraries are becoming more popular in many countries.

qs.ex: 直後の文で「あまりお金を使わずに多くの道具を使える」と説明しているので、「お金の節約に役立つ」。
お金の節約・人のつながりという理由を受けて「こうした理由で人気が高まっている」とまとめています。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Sarah Wilson
To: Natsumi Kato
Date: January 15
Subject: Volunteering at the animal shelter

Hi Natsumi,
Do you remember the animal shelter near the station? I've been volunteering there every Saturday since last fall. I walk the dogs, clean their rooms, and play with the cats. It's hard work, but I love it. Last week, the manager told me that they need more volunteers. Would you like to join me?
Before you start, you need to go to a one-hour training session. The next session is on January 25 at 2 p.m. During the session, the staff will explain how to take care of the animals safely. You'll also need a letter from one of your parents because you're under 18.
By the way, the shelter is going to hold an adoption event in March. Families who want to take a dog or cat home can meet the animals there. I'm going to help make posters for it. If you join us, maybe you can help, too!
Your friend,
Sarah

qs.q: What does Sarah want Natsumi to do?
o: Adopt a cat from the shelter.
Volunteer at the animal shelter with her.
Give her a letter from her parents.
qs.ex: Would you like to join me?(いっしょにやらない?)と誘っています。

qs.q: Before Natsumi starts volunteering, she has to
o: meet the manager at the station.
qs.ex: Before you start, you need to go to a one-hour training session. とあります。

qs.q: What will happen at the shelter in March?
o: Families will be able to meet animals they may take home.
The shelter will move to a new place.
A new training session will start.
qs.ex: adoption event(引き取りのイベント)で、家族が動物と会えます。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: The Story of the "Black Box"
blocks.body:
When a plane has an accident, investigators want to know what happened. One of the most important tools for them is the flight recorder, often called the "black box." It records information about the flight, such as the plane's speed and height, and the voices of the pilots in the cockpit.
The idea for this device came from an Australian scientist named David Warren. In the 1950s, several new passenger jets crashed, and nobody could find out why. Warren thought that a recording of the cockpit might help. He also had a personal reason to care about plane safety. When he was a boy, his father had died in a plane crash.
At first, many people were not interested in Warren's invention. Some pilots did not like the idea of being recorded while they were working. They felt that someone would always be listening to them. However, as more accidents were studied, people began to understand how useful the recordings were. Over time, countries started to require flight recorders on large planes.
Today, flight recorders are built to survive fire, strong impacts, and deep water. Interestingly, these "black boxes" are not black at all. They are painted bright orange so that searchers can find them more easily after an accident. Thanks to the information they keep, experts have been able to make flying safer for everyone.

qs.q: Why did David Warren think a cockpit recording might help?
o: Pilots wanted to listen to music during flights.
People could not find the causes of some plane crashes.
Planes were becoming too fast to control.
Passengers wanted to talk to the pilots.
qs.ex: 新しいジェット機の事故の原因がわからなかったからです。

qs.q: Some pilots did not like the flight recorder because
o: it was too heavy for planes.
they felt someone would always be listening to them.
it made the cockpit too noisy.
qs.ex: 仕事中の会話をいつも聞かれていると感じたからです。

qs.q: Why are flight recorders painted bright orange?
o: To make them look like black boxes.
To show which company made them.
To make them easier to find.
qs.ex: so that searchers can find them more easily とあります。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: David Warren's father died in a plane crash.
Flight recorders were first used in the 1920s.
All pilots welcomed the flight recorder at once.
Flight recorders cannot survive deep water.
qs.ex: When he was a boy, his father had died in a plane crash. とあります。

parts.prompt:
あなたは、外国人の知り合い(Jamie)から、Eメールで質問を受け取りました。この質問にわかりやすく答える返信メールを英文で書きなさい。
あなたが書く返信メールの中で、Jamieのメールの下線部(vegetable garden)について、あなたがより理解を深めるために、下線部の特徴を問う具体的な質問を2つしなさい。
返信は「Hi, Jamie! Thank you for your e-mail.」で始まり「Best wishes,」で終わります(この部分は書かなくてよい)。
parts.body:
Hi!
Guess what? My family and I started a [vegetable garden] in our backyard last month. Growing vegetables is a lot of fun, and they taste much better than the ones from the supermarket. I want to grow something new next year. What vegetable do you think is good for me to grow?
Your friend,
Jamie
rules: 語数の目安は40語〜50語です。
Jamieの質問に答えること、下線部(vegetable garden)について質問を2つすることの両方が必要です。
parts.model: I think tomatoes are good for you to grow. They are easy to take care of, and you can use them in many dishes. By the way, I want to know more about your garden. How big is it? And what vegetables are you growing now?
checks: Jamieの質問(何を育てるとよいか)に答えている
答えの理由も書いている
vegetable garden について具体的な質問を2つしている(How big…? What vegetables…? など)
語数が40〜50語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(Eメール)

parts.prompt:
あなたは、外国人の知り合いから以下のQUESTIONをされました。QUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。

QUESTION
Do you think it is a good idea for students to use tablets in class?
rules: 語数の目安は50語〜60語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
QUESTIONに答えていない場合や、内容がQUESTIONからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I think it is a good idea for students to use tablets in class. I have two reasons. First, students can find information quickly on the Internet. Second, tablets are lighter than paper textbooks, so students do not have to carry heavy bags to school every day. For these reasons, I agree with this idea.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
First, Second, For these reasons などで構成がわかる
語数が50〜60語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, Emma. Are you ready for the math test tomorrow?
Not really. I don't understand the last chapter.
Do you want to study together after school?
o: Sure, that would help a lot.
items.ex: 一緒に勉強しようと誘われて「うん、すごく助かる」。

lines: Excuse me, does this bus stop at City Hall?
No, you need to take the number 5.
o: At the stop across the street.
items.ex: Where(どこで)なので場所を答えます。

lines: Mom, have you seen my math notebook?
o: Maybe you left it at school.
items.ex: 机にないなら「学校に置いてきたのかも」。

lines: Hi, I'd like to change my reservation from Friday to Saturday.
Certainly. May I have your name, please?
items.ex: 名前をたずねられているので名前を答えます。

lines: Dad, can I borrow your camera for the school trip?
Sure. Just be careful with it.
I will. Where is the charger?
o: In the drawer by the TV.
items.ex: 充電器の場所を答えています。

lines: Why don't we get some lunch?
o: Good idea. Where should we go?
items.ex: Why don't we ～?(～しない?)の誘いに「いいね。どこに行く?」。

lines: Ms. Lee, I couldn't finish my essay.
I was sick for three days.
o: OK. You can hand it in next Monday.
items.ex: 病気だった生徒に提出をのばしてあげています。

lines: Are you going to the fireworks festival?
I want to, but I don't have anyone to go with.
Why don't you come with my family?
items.ex: 誘いを喜んで受けています。

lines: Excuse me, I think you dropped this.
Oh, my scarf! Thank you so much.
You're welcome. It was on the floor by the door.
items.ex: 落とし物を拾ってもらい「もっと気をつけます」。

lines: How was your first week at your new school?
It was OK. Everyone is nice.
o: My school is near the station.
Yes, a boy in my class.
items.ex: 友達ができたか→「うん、クラスの男の子と」。

lines: Hi, Tom. Are you going to the basketball game on Friday?
I wanted to, but I have to work at my part-time job.
I asked, but nobody could switch with me.
items.q: Why can't Tom go to the basketball game?
items.ex: アルバイトのシフトを代われる人がいませんでした。

lines: Excuse me. I'd like to return this coffee maker.
Is there a problem with it?
Yes. It makes strange noises, and the coffee isn't hot.
I see. Would you like a new one or your money back?
items.q: What will the man do?
items.ex: I'll take my money back.(返金してもらう)と言っています。

lines: Mom, Kate invited me to her house this Saturday.
That sounds fun. But don't forget your piano lesson at ten.
I know. I'll go to Kate's after the lesson.
items.q: What will the girl do first on Saturday?
items.ex: ピアノのレッスンのあとで Kate の家に行きます。

lines: Hello. I'm calling about the apartment on Oak Street. Is it still available?
Yes, it is. Would you like to see it?
Yes. Can I come tomorrow afternoon?
items.q: Why is the man calling?
o: To ask for directions to Oak Street.
items.ex: アパートがまだ空いているか問い合わせています。

lines: Ms. Davis, I want to join the volunteer club.
Great! We clean the park every Sunday morning.
Every Sunday? I have soccer practice on some Sundays.
That's OK. Just come when you can.
items.q: What does the volunteer club do?
items.ex: We clean the park every Sunday morning. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me. I ordered the chicken salad, but this is a tuna salad.
I'm very sorry. I'll bring you the right one right away.
Thank you. Could you also bring some more water?
items.q: What is the woman's problem?
items.ex: 注文とちがうサラダが来ました。

lines: Honey, have you seen the car keys?
I think they're in your jacket.
Then look on the kitchen table. You came in through the kitchen last night.
items.q: Where will the man look for the keys next?
items.ex: Then look on the kitchen table. と言われています。

lines: Excuse me. I'm looking for a book called The Silent Sea.
Let me check. It's checked out right now. It should be back next Tuesday.
Sure. Just write your name here.
items.q: What will the girl probably do?
o: Read it in the library today.
items.ex: 予約できるか聞いて、名前を書くように言われています。

lines: Did you hear that the swimming pool will close next month?
They're going to repair it. It'll be closed for three months.
Oh no. I'll have to find another pool.
items.q: Why will the pool close?
items.ex: They're going to repair it.(修理する)と言っています。

lines: Dad, I want to buy a new bike. My old one is too small.
How much is the bike you want?
That's a lot. I'll pay half if you save the other half.
items.q: How much money will the boy need to save?
items.ex: 300ドルの半分を父が払うので、残り半分の150ドルです。

lines: Jessica works at a bank. Every morning, she takes the train to work, but last week the trains stopped because of heavy snow. She had to stay home and work on her computer. She found it convenient, so now she works from home on Fridays.
items.q: What does Jessica do on Fridays now?
o: She takes the train to the bank.
items.ex: now she works from home on Fridays とあります。

lines: Attention, passengers. Flight 208 to Sydney has been delayed because of a problem with the plane. The new departure time is 4:30 p.m. Passengers can get a free drink at the café near Gate 12. We are sorry for the trouble.
items.q: What can passengers do near Gate 12?
items.ex: Passengers can get a free drink at the café near Gate 12. とあります。

lines: Did you know that honeybees dance? When a bee finds flowers with a lot of food, it goes back to its home and dances. The dance tells the other bees which direction to fly and how far away the flowers are. In this way, bees can share information.
items.q: Why do honeybees dance?
o: To tell other bees where food is.
items.ex: ダンスでえさのある方向と距離を仲間に伝えます。

lines: Ryan wanted to learn to cook, so he joined a cooking class at a community center. At first, he burned everything. But his teacher gave him useful advice, and now he can make several dishes. Next month, he will cook dinner for his parents' anniversary.
items.q: What will Ryan do next month?
items.ex: 両親の結婚記念日に夕食を作ります。

lines: Thank you for visiting City Museum. Our special exhibition about ancient Egypt is on the third floor. Please note that taking photos is not allowed in the exhibition room. The museum shop on the first floor sells postcards of the exhibition.
items.q: What is not allowed in the exhibition room?
items.ex: taking photos is not allowed とあります。

lines: Emily's grandmother lives alone in the countryside. Emily used to visit her only once a year. But last year, Emily's grandmother learned how to use a tablet. Now they have video calls every Sunday, and her grandmother shows her the vegetables she grows.
items.q: What happens every Sunday?
o: Emily and her grandmother have video calls.
items.ex: Now they have video calls every Sunday とあります。

lines: In Japan, many people eat eel in summer. There is a special day for eating eel called "Doyo no Ushi no Hi." People believe that eel gives them energy during the hot season. However, the number of eels is decreasing, so some stores now sell other kinds of fish on that day.
items.q: Why do some stores sell other kinds of fish?
o: Eel is too difficult to cook.
The number of eels is decreasing.
Eel is not good in summer.
items.ex: the number of eels is decreasing とあります。

lines: Kevin is a high school student. He wanted to buy a guitar, so he started working at a supermarket on weekends. After six months, he had enough money. Now he practices every evening and hopes to play at the school festival in the fall.
items.q: How did Kevin get money for his guitar?
o: His parents gave it to him.
items.ex: 週末にスーパーで働いてお金をためました。

lines: Good morning, everyone. Today's school trip to the science museum will start at 9 a.m. Please meet in front of the school gate by 8:45. Don't forget to bring your lunch, because there are no restaurants near the museum.
items.q: Why should students bring their lunch?
o: There are no restaurants near the museum.
The museum is closed at lunchtime.
Lunch at the museum is expensive.
They will eat on the bus.
items.ex: there are no restaurants near the museum とあります。

lines: Last weekend, Nancy went hiking with her friends. Halfway up the mountain, it started to rain. They decided to go back down because the path was dangerous. Nancy was disappointed, but she plans to try again next month.
items.q: Why did Nancy and her friends go back down the mountain?
items.ex: 雨が降り出して道が危なくなったからです。
